 Order
Petitioner is the accused in SC No.196/2024 on the files of Fast Track Special Court, Chengannoor.

He faces criminal prosecution for the criminal offences under Sections 376, 376(2)(n), 377, 506(i),
323 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 119(1) (b) of Kerala Police Act, 2011.
The allegation against the petitioner is that he committed rape of the de facto complainant on various occasions from the month of March 2021 onwards till 11.05.2023.
It is stated that both the de facto complainant and the accused were working in the Health department of Kerala State, and thus they got acquainted with each other.

The specific allegation of the petitioner is that on the first instance of rape which took place in the month of March 2021, the petitioner overpowered her and committed rape, and thereafter took her nude photographs.

The subsequent instances of rape are said to have been committed by the petitioner by subjecting her to blackmailing and by threatening her that he would publish her nude photographs and compromising postures on social media.

Thus,
the accused is alleged to have committed the aforesaid offences.
In the present petition, the petitioner would contend that none of the offences as alleged by the prosecution are attracted in the facts and circumstances of the case.
It is stated that the petitioner and the de facto complainant were having consensual sexual relationship on all those instances referred in the complaint of the survivor.

It is further pointed out that the prolonged period of more than two years of continued instances of rape would itself show that the relationship between the Shaji vs State Of Kerala on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118676733/
2 parties was consensual.
3. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.

4. As already stated above, this is a case where the definite case of the de facto complainant is that at the first instance, the petitioner overpowered her and resorted to forceful sexual intercourse with her, and thereafter took her nude photographs and images of compromising postures.

On all subsequent instances, according to the de facto complainant, she was compelled to accede to the demand of the petitioner to go to rooms and other buildings and surrender 2025:KER:39885 CRL.MC NO. 3675 OF 2025 her body to him as a consequence of the emotional blackmailing committed by the petitioner who said that her nude photographs and images of compromising postures he had recorded, would be published in social media and displayed to her friends and relatives.

Thus it could be seen that the de facto complainant has got a plausible explanation for the reason why she had gone along with the petitioner on subsequent occasions, despite having the very harrowing experience which happened in the month of March 2021.
The question whether the version of the de facto complainant in the above regard could be believed or not, is a matter to be decided by the trial court.
This Court, while exercising its inherent powers under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), cannot sit on judgment over the reliability of the version of the prosecutrix.
As the matter stands now, the relevant materials garnered by the Investigating Agency would clearly bring home the offence of rape alleged against the petitioner.
There is absolutely no reason to interfere with the final report, and to terminate the prosecution proceedings at this stage.
Therefore, I am of the view that the request in this petition to quash the proceedings against the petitioner, cannot be entertained.
In the result, the petition is hereby dismissed.
